description: Hi! We're the Scribes of Ether, scholars with a burning passion for knowledge and we intend to breach the boundary between the known and unknown through our literary journey.
summary:
An Echo of Exploration: Their Missions Ended. Their Stories Didn't.

Echoes of Exploration is an interactive educational archive in story format to put forgotten exploratory gear on display. It is a prototype of a digital-museum presentation that functions as a click-through, developed to display five NASA objects that were placed on the Moon and Mars: Surveyor 3, ALSEP, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity.

The project is a process of converting technical NASA mission data into stories that young kids and seasoned space fanciers can understand. The Presentation bring to your attention the reasons for their deployment, what scientific results came from them, what they helped discover and what happened after their mission. The scientific foundation is provided by NASA's NSSDCA, NASA Science, NASA/JPL mission records and historical documentation, which visitors can check to investigate further for themselves.

We want to create historical moments in space that are easy to enjoy, Honor the accomplishments of a fleet of robots, and promote the value of science and engineering to other worlds.
details: An Interactive Story based Digital Museum, Echoes of Exploration unveils and re-introduces to the public some of the more obscure NASA space exploration equipment. Our presentation is a prototype 7 slide clickable show with 5 historical artifacts of the Moon and Mars that we chose: Surveyor 3, ALSEP, Sojourner, Opportunity and Ingenuity. The project's role is to make the stories of NASA missions easily accessible to school-age kids as well as space buffs and the casual Space enthusiast. Users can uncover the original function, scientific accomplishments, mission history and end-of-mission status of each artifact along with links clicking to the NASA artifacts source documents. We use data and resources from NASA's Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), NASA Science, NASA/JPL, and NASA's historical archives. This presentation has been created with python and Python-pptx library and can be viewed and edited with MS PowerPoint. There was no additional hardware needed. Our creative approach uses science information as stories, and makes the technical mission record into an engaging digital exhibit. Educational usability, scientific correctness, navigation, and the distinction of equipment deliberately forgotten on space vehicles, but which then lost its mission capabilities, were taken into consideration. We are hoping to contribute to the heritage of robotic explorers, pursue space exploration history more accessible, preserve, promote and build curiosity in planetary science and encourage the next generation of space explorers.
